title: Geometric finite Kummer comparison and base change
statement: Assume the finite arithmetic data at level n gives a ring map a from Z/ell^(N+1) to A and an additive coordinate isomorphism b that is linear for a. For every scheme T where ell is invertible, the normalized finite Tate-line isomorphism A(1)_T ≅ mu_(ell^(N+1),T) tensor A exists and is uniquely characterized on local pure tensors by the N-th root projection. It is compatible with the derived tensor comparison and with arbitrary base change, including the root-limit map and the commuting tensor square.

source.place: Proof steps (3)--(5), normalized projection, derived tensor and base-change clauses

proof.text: Set $L_T=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T$ and $M_{N,T}=L_T\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T}(R_N)_T$. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] (3), specialized to $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, uniformizer $\ell$ and level $N$, $M_{N,T}$ is locally free of rank one over $(R_N)_T$; these are exactly the scalar extensions of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. We verify that the particular map $\rho_{N,T}:M_{N,T}\to\mu_{\ell^N,T}$, $x\otimes\bar a\mapsto a\,p_N(x)$, is an isomorphism, rather than merely using an unspecified isomorphism of the two lines. The balanced tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] identifies $M_{N,T}$ with $L_T/\ell^N L_T$: the inverse maps are $x\otimes\bar a\mapsto a[x]$ and $[x]\mapsto x\otimes1$, with lifts of $\bar a$ chosen locally; changing a lift contributes $\ell^N[x]=0$. The inverse limit is sectionwise [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Write a section $x$ of $\ker p_N$ multiplicatively as $(x_r)$, so $x_N=1$. Then $y_r=x_{r+N}$ belongs to $\mu_{\ell^r}$ because $x_{r+N}^{\ell^r}=x_N=1$, the $y_r$ are compatible, and $\ell^Ny=x$. Conversely $p_N(\ell^Ny)=1$ for every $y$. Thus $\ker p_N=\ell^NL_T$, and $\rho_{N,T}$ is a monomorphism. Trivialize $M_{N,T}$ and $\mu_{\ell^N,T}$ together using (3) and (1) of the cited Tate-line lemma. The map between the two constant $R_N$-lines is multiplication by a locally constant scalar $a$; refine the cover until $a$ is constant. On a nonempty member of this cover, a nonunit $a\in R_N$ is divisible by $\ell$ and annihilates the nonzero constant section $\ell^{N-1}$, contradicting monicity. On an empty member both module sheaves are zero, so the comparison is already an isomorphism. Hence $a$ is a unit on every member of this cover and $\rho_{N,T}$ is an isomorphism. This proves the required projection formula without identifying the completed coefficient sheaf with the constant sheaf.

The two successive scalar extensions in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] identify $A(1)_T$ with $L_T\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T}A_T$. Here the explicit associativity maps are $(x\otimes b)\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes ba$ and $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a$. Since $\ell^N A=0$, the balanced tensor relations give mutually inverse maps
$$L_T\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}A_T\longleftrightarrow (L_T\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}(R_N)_T)\otimes_{(R_N)_T}A_T,$$
$$x\otimes a\longmapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a,\qquad (x\otimes\bar b)\otimes a\longmapsto x\otimes\bar b a.$$
Changing a lift of $\bar b$ changes the latter by a multiple of $\ell^N a=0$. These formulas first define maps of presheaf tensor products and then of their sheafifications [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; checking them on pure tensors proves that they are inverse. Compose with $\rho_{N,T}\otimes1$ from step 3. This proves the asserted canonical isomorphism $\alpha_T$, explicitly $x\otimes a\mapsto p_N(x)\otimes a$.

By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] (1), $\mu_{\ell^N,T}$ is locally free of rank one over $(R_N)_T$. On a trivializing cover, tensoring with it is the identity functor on module sheaves. Thus it preserves exactness: a section in a kernel can locally be lifted from the preceding term on that cover, and equalities are checked locally. This is flatness as defined by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. By [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] this sheaf in degree zero is K-flat. Consequently the ordinary tensor on the right of $\alpha_T$ is also $\mu_{\ell^N,T}\otimes^L_{R_N}A_T$, by [def-weil-derived-tensor], with the canonical augmentation given by the degree-zero model. Put $B_T=\mu_{\ell^N,T}\otimes_{(R_N)_T}A_T$. On the same trivializing cover $B_T$ is $A_T$, so tensoring over $A_T$ with $B_T$ restricts to the identity on that cover. For any exact sequence, a section of a kernel therefore locally has a preimage from the preceding term, and these local image conditions prove exactness of its tensor sequence. Thus $B_T$ is flat over $A_T$; the isomorphism $A(1)_T\cong B_T$ makes tensoring with $A(1)_T$ isomorphic to this exact functor. Both are K-flat in degree zero by the cited bounded-above criterion. Tensoring termwise with either line therefore computes the derived twist of any complex of $A_T$-modules. Applying the derived tensor bifunctor to $\alpha_T$ gives the comparison naturally in that complex. The $R_N$-flat sheaf in the first calculation is $\mu_{\ell^N,T}$; the $A_T$-flat sheaves in the twist calculation are $B_T$ and $A(1)_T$.

Use the constant-sheaf resolution $C=[R\xrightarrow{\ell^N}R]\to(R_N)_T$ of [lem-pur-constant-two-term-resolution], with $R=(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T$. Multiplication by $\ell^N$ on $L_T$ is injective: if $x=(x_r)$ satisfies $x_r^{\ell^N}=1$ for all $r$, then $x_r=x_{r+N}^{\ell^N}=1$ for every $r$, using the sectionwise limit [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Hence that lemma gives a quasi-isomorphism $L_T\otimes_R C\to(L_T\otimes_R(R_N)_T)[0]$. Its augmentation on degree-zero cohomology is the quotient projection, which step 3 identifies with $p_N:L_T\to\mu_{\ell^N,T}$.

proof.text: Choose a bounded-above flat resolution $q:P\to L_T[0]$ by [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement]; it is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Apply [lem-pur-kflat-cone-comparison] with $M=(R_N)_T$ and the resolution $C$ from step 6. Its bottom arrow is the quasi-isomorphism just proved. The lemma's commuting augmentation square therefore identifies the canonical comparison $L_T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(R_N)_T\to(L_T\otimes_R(R_N)_T)[0]$ as an isomorphism, with the quotient augmentation used in step 3.

source.place: Proof; expanded finite-level reduction argument; constant-coefficient resolution and augmentation repair

proof.text: Choose the finite basis $A\cong R_N^{ef}$ from step 2. Its inclusions and projections give $A_T\cong((R_N)_T)^{\oplus ef}$ and the resolution $D=C^{\oplus ef}\to A_T$. Under the tensor relations [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $x\otimes(a_i)_i\mapsto(x\otimes a_i)_i$ has inverse given by summing the basis inclusions; these maps commute with differentials and augmentations. Kernels and images of a finite sum of differentials are computed componentwise, so both $D\to A_T$ and $L_T\otimes_R D\to(L_T\otimes_R A_T)[0]$ are quasi-isomorphisms by step 6. Each term of $D$ is finite free; tensoring with it is a finite sum of identity functors, whose kernels and images are componentwise, so it is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Thus $D$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Apply the augmentation-square conclusion of [lem-pur-kflat-cone-comparison] to $q:P\to L_T[0]$ and $D\to A_T$: the canonical comparison $L_T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A_T\to(L_T\otimes_R A_T)[0]$ is an isomorphism. Step 4 identifies its target with $B_T$ by $x\otimes a\mapsto p_N(x)\otimes a$. The basis verifies invertibility; the augmentation maps were defined without it.

proof.text: We spell out finite-root base change on the pro-etale site. Let $h:T'\to T$ be any morphism and $m=\ell^r$, $r\geq1$. Put $W_m=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbf Z[z]/(z^m-1))$ and $V_{m,T}=T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}W_m$, using the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. On an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset T$, the fibre-product universal property and [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identify $V_{m,T}\times_TU$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B[z]/(z^m-1))$: compatible ring maps from $B$ and $\mathbf Z[z]/(z^m-1)$ are exactly a $B$-algebra map from this polynomial quotient. A map from an affine scheme into this root scheme is exactly an element $z$ satisfying $z^m=1$, whose inverse is $z^{m-1}$. For any scheme $Q\to T$, cover $Q$ by affine opens mapping into affine opens of $T$; the maps determined by a global root agree on every affine open of each overlap, since their ring maps send $z$ to that same restricted root. They glue uniquely by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Conversely a morphism gives these compatible local roots, which glue by the structure-sheaf axiom. This proves that $V_{m,T}$ represents the root functor [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], without assuming $T$ affine. Apply [lem-sbc-root-split-away-cover-etale] on each affine chart with $g=1$ and exponent $m$; $D(1)$ is the whole chart and $m$ is invertible. The affine-local criterion in [def-weil-etale-morphism] now shows that $V_{m,T}\to T$ is etale, since the displayed affine root charts cover its source and their bases cover $T$. It is an object of the pro-etale site by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]; its represented functor is a sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-subcanonical]. Finally the fibre-product universal property identifies $T'\times_TV_{m,T}$ with $V_{m,T'}$: a map into either object is exactly a map into $T'$ together with a compatible map into $W_m$. This identification retains the coordinate $z$.

proof.text:
For an object $V$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, its base change $V'=T'\times_TV$ is the object used by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For every sheaf $G$ on $T'_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the adjunction and [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(h^{-1}h_V,G)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_V,h_*G)=(h_*G)(V)=G(V')=\operatorname{Hom}(h_{V'},G).$$
The represented presheaves are sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-subcanonical]. Write $\Phi_G$ for this chain of bijections. The criterion [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] gives an isomorphism $\theta:h_{V'}\to h^{-1}h_V$ with $\Phi_G(f)=f\theta$. Let $\delta:h^{-1}h_V\to h_{V'}$ be adjoint to the map $h_V\to h_*h_{V'}$ sending $a:Q\to V$ to $\mathrm{id}_{T'}\times_Ta:T'\times_TQ\to V'$. Evaluating this adjoint at $\mathrm{id}_V$ shows $\Phi_{h_{V'}}(\delta)=\mathrm{id}_{h_{V'}}$. Thus $\delta\theta=\mathrm{id}$, so $\delta=\theta^{-1}$ is precisely the canonical isomorphism $h^{-1}h_V\to h_{V'}$. Apply this to the global root scheme $V_{\ell^r,T}$ of step 9. We obtain $\beta_{r,h}:h^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{\ell^r,T'}$. Under the Hom bijections its adjoint sends a root $z$ on $Q\to T$ to its image under the global-section ring map for $T'\times_TQ\to Q$. This is precisely the comparison map of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image]. That ring map sends $zz'$ to the product of their images and $z^j$ to the $j$-th power of the image. Thus $\beta_{r,h}$ respects the group law and the scalar action, and for $t_r:z\mapsto z^\ell$ one has $t'_r\beta_{r+1,h}=\beta_{r,h}h^{-1}t_r$. For $g:T''\to T'$, the ring maps for the two projections compose to the ring map for $T''\times_TQ\to Q$, so, under the inverse-image composition identification, $\beta_{r,h\circ g}=\beta_{r,g}\,g^{-1}\beta_{r,h}$. The projection for the identity map is the identity, giving $\beta_{r,\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$. These formulas prove the transition, identity and composition compatibilities explicitly.

Apply [lem-pur-tate-inverse-limit-base-change] to $F_{r,S}=\mu_{\ell^r,S}$ and the transition-, scalar-, identity- and composition-compatible maps $\beta_{r,h}$ of step 10. The canonical constant-ring identifications, including $\mathbf Z_\ell$, are supplied by [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. In the lemma's notation $B_S=A(1)_S$ by step 4, and its $\alpha_S$ is exactly that step's projection-tensor map. The lemma gives $c_h$, its linearity and composition laws, and $\alpha_{T'}b_h=(\beta_{N,h}\otimes1)h^{-1}\alpha_T$. Both $\alpha$ maps are isomorphisms by step 4, so the lemma also gives that $b_h$ is an isomorphism, with its identity and composition laws.

Finally [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] says that module pullback for the finite constant ring $A$ is exact, so its derived pullback is termwise inverse image with the coefficient action identified by the canonical ring isomorphism. Put $B_T=\mu_{\ell^N,T}\otimes_{(R_N)_T}A_T$ and $d_h=\beta_{N,h}\otimes1:h^{-1}B_T\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{T'}$. For any $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], with $R=A_T$ and $S=A_{T'}$, identifies the pullbacks of $K\otimes_A^L A(1)_T$ and $K\otimes_A^L B_T$ with $h^{-1}K\otimes_A^L h^{-1}A(1)_T$ and $h^{-1}K\otimes_A^L h^{-1}B_T$, respectively. Bifunctoriality and the equation $\alpha_{T'}b_h=d_h h^{-1}\alpha_T$ in step 11 give
$$ (1\otimes^L\alpha_{T'})(1\otimes^Lb_h)=(1\otimes^Ld_h)(1\otimes^Lh^{-1}\alpha_T). $$
The coefficient lines $A(1)_T,B_T$ are flat over $A_T$ and K-flat in degree zero by step 5, so these derived tensors can be computed by termwise tensoring $K$ with the lines. On each term the displayed equation is exactly the pure-tensor equation of step 11; the maps commute with the differentials because they act as the identity on $K$. Thus the ordinary and derived comparisons agree, naturally in $K$. This is the asserted joint compatibility with derived tensor and base change.
